name: Creme Brulee
desc: Vanilla custard thickened on the stove, baked, chilled, and finished with a broiled sugar crust.

source.title: Crème Brûlée
source.evidence: Identical five ingredients and amounts (6 yolks, 6 tbsp sugar divided, 1/2 tsp vanilla, 2 1/2 cups cream, 2 tbsp brown sugar) and the same double boiler, 300°F bake and broiler method.

ingredients.raw: 6 tbsp granulated sugar, divided (4 tbsp + 2 tbsp)

steps: Whisk the egg yolks, 4 tbsp granulated sugar and the vanilla in a bowl until thick and creamy.
Heat the cream in a saucepan over low heat, stirring, until it is steaming and almost boiling.
Slowly whisk the hot cream into the yolk mixture until combined.
Pour into the top of a double boiler set over simmering water. Stir until the custard lightly coats the back of a spoon, about 3 minutes.
Pour into a shallow heatproof baking dish or 5 ramekins. Bake about 30 minutes, until set at the edges but still slightly jiggly in the center.
Cool to room temperature, then refrigerate at least 1 hour or overnight.
Heat the broiler. Mix the remaining 2 tbsp granulated sugar with the brown sugar and sprinkle it evenly over the custard.
Broil about 2 minutes, watching constantly, until the sugar melts and caramelizes. Cool slightly, then refrigerate about 10 minutes to set the custard again before serving.
tips: A kitchen torch gives more even control than the broiler and keeps the custard underneath cold.

references.title: Crème Brûlée
references.usedFor: slightly jiggly doneness cue, 3 minute double boiler time, post-broil chill, yield
